name: Dequeue watch
sheds_why: BH-7509: it clears the merge queue, so it keeps running while the hub is over. Its one spend is a dqw_llm_classify call per dequeued PR, not a build or an agent session.

knobs.note: BH-3719: read by bin/dequeue-watch.sh as ${DEQUEUE_WATCH:-1}: 0 writes ` disabled` and stops before any read.

BH-3719: 0 is observe mode. Each dequeue is still classified and claimed as action `observe`, and the would-be action is logged as WOULD_<ACTION> in logs/dequeue-watch.log with no side effect. Flipping to 1 takes over the observe rows. BH-3859: the lane ships at 0 (registry, code fallback and the schema seed row), posts one observe report after DEQUEUE_WATCH_OBSERVE_TICKS ticks, and never flips itself. To let it act: bin/harness-ctl.sh set dequeue-watch DEQUEUE_WATCH_ACT 1.

BH-3859: observe ticks before the one observe report (12 = 1h at */5). The report is a warn with id observe-report:dequeue-watch, sent once, carrying the WOULD_ summary and the flip command. Counter in state/observe-report/dequeue-watch.json on the hub.
Fix rounds per (PR, class) across heads before dequeue-watch holds the PR for a person.
Minutes a dequeued head may go with no dequeue-watch action owning it before the watchdog pages critical (dqw-unowned:).
Dequeued PRs per project per tick. Past it the rest wait for the next tick and one dqw-page-cut: warn says how many.
Bytes of the failed batch's `gh run view --log-failed` output read per PR.
FAIL lines kept per dequeue for the classifier, the event row and the fix-round brief.
Comma/space list of classes that always hold for a person instead of getting a fix round. Empty holds only past DEQUEUE_WATCH_FIX_ROUNDS.
1 asks the dequeue.classify model about a dequeue the rules leave unclassified with FAIL lines. 0 sends it straight to a hold.
Budget in dollars for one dequeue.classify call.
Overrides the dequeue.classify route's model for this lane. Empty uses the route.

0 makes this lane call no model at all. bin/lib/llm-gate.sh refuses BEFORE the vendor call and writes a zero-cost row_source=refused row, so the stop is visible in the ledger rather than being a lane that went quiet.

Comma/space list of the ONLY ladder rungs this lane may reach. Empty is every rung, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. A rung outside the list is refused before the call, so a cliff or a failure on the standing lane cannot descend into one that costs ~100x (#1141, the $793 descent).

Dollars this lane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend — never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. A second, project-scoped ceiling is the lane.<id>.<project>.llm_usd_cap_day row, which is read only when somebody wrote it. Registry default 0 like every LLM lane (tests/llm-lane-knobs.bh-2533); this lane calls dequeue.classify only for a dequeue the rules leave unclassified with FAIL lines, at most once per failure fingerprint. Set lane.dequeue-watch.llm_usd_cap_day for a daily ceiling.
Test seam: a file bin/dequeue-watch.sh sources after its libs, only when HARNESS_TEST_SANDBOX=1. NOT settable from the control plane: it names a file a root lane sources.
BH-3859 test seam: the tick timeout in seconds, read by bin/dequeue-watch.sh only when HARNESS_TEST_SANDBOX=1. Prod is always 240. NOT settable from the control plane.
Test seam gate: bin/dequeue-watch.sh sources DEQUEUE_WATCH_FIXTURE only when this is 1 (the test harness sets it). Never set on a box, and NOT settable from the control plane.
